chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the fasting of the day of Al-Fitr, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting to fast it, nor the fasting of the days of Al-Tashreeq.'

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Al-Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: It is not befitting (indicating makruh/disliked status)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting during Eid al-Fitr and the Days of Tashreeq in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Samaanah reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declared fasting on Eid al-Fitr and the Days of Tashreeq as *makruh* (disliked) rather than strictly prohibited, reflecting the Shia view that these are days of celebration and feasting. This ruling aligns with the Prophetic tradition of abstaining from voluntary fasts during these specific periods to emphasize joy and gratitude for the completion of Ramadan or the Hajj rituals. The distinction between *makruh* and *haram* highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary acts of worship during festive times.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasts of the day of Al-Fitr (Eid), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting to Fast it, nor Fasting the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> & 13<sup>th</sup> Zil Hijja)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said

the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about fasting on the day of al-Fitr (first day of the month of Shawwal). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not proper to fast as well as on the days of al- Tashriq.’”
